data.name: Namias
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew word ‘na’im’, meaning ‘pleasant’ or ‘delightful’, the name Namias is associated with the protection and welfare of the people. This name holds biblical significance as it is mentioned in the Old Testament Book of Isaiah, where God promises to be a shield and a wall, a fortress and a refuge from the storm and the fear of the enemy.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name representing God's protection and care for His people.

historical_references.reference: According to legend, Namias was a shepherdess who lived in the region of Galilee during the time of Jesus. She was renowned for her piety and devotion, and was said to have been visited by the infant Jesus, who left the mark of the cross on her forehead as a sign of his favor.

Saint Namias of Rome was a martyr during the Diocletian Persecution in the late 3rd century AD. She was a deaconess and was imprisoned and tortured for her refusal to sacrifice to Roman gods. She was eventually executed by being buried alive in a pit.
